tldr: MapCoder is a multi-agent prompting framework that replicates the human program synthesis cycle through retrieval, planning, coding, and debugging agents, achieving new state-of-the-art pass@1 results across multiple code generation benchmarks.
contributions: Introduction of MapCoder, a multi-agent code generation approach that mimics the human programming cycle (recalling examples, planning, code generation, debugging).
An autonomous retrieval agent that generates relevant problem-solving examples without manual crafting or external retrieval models.
A novel structured pipeline with dynamic agent traversal and a debugging agent that uses only sample I/O without generating additional test cases.
Comprehensive evaluation across eight benchmarks showing significant improvements over direct prompting and existing methods like Reflexion and AlphaCodium.
methods: MapCoder employs four LLM agents in a cascaded pipeline: a Retrieval Agent that generates k similar problems and their metadata, a Planning Agent that creates step-by-step plans with confidence scores for each retrieved example, a Coding Agent that translates the highest-confidence plan into code, and a Debugging Agent that fixes bugs using sample I/O. The system uses an adaptive traversal schema where code failing sample tests is iteratively debugged up to t times per plan, cycling through plans if needed. Prompts are carefully designed for each agent, incorporating analogical principles and explicit algorithmic guidance. Evaluation uses the Pass@k metric with k=5 for HumanEval and k=3 for other datasets, testing on ChatGPT, GPT-4, Gemini Pro, and Mistral-7B-instruct.
results: MapCoder achieves new state-of-the-art pass@1 results: HumanEval 93.9% (GPT-4), MBPP 83.1%, APPS 22.0%, CodeContests 28.5%, and xCodeEval 45.3%. On CodeContest, MapCoder's Pass@5 (35.2% with GPT-4) matches AlphaCodium's Pass@1 (29%). Improvements over direct prompting range from 41.3% to 132.8% on competitive datasets for ChatGPT and 73.7% to 135.1% for GPT-4. The framework consistently outperforms baselines like Reflexion and Self-collaboration across both simple and complex problem sets.
limitations: Performance drops are observed with certain self-reflection approaches when AI-generated test cases are incorrect (e.g., 26.3% drop with ChatGPT on HumanEval when replacing GPT-4). The system's effectiveness may vary across different base models, with GPT-4 generally scaling higher than ChatGPT. The complexity of the approach is O(kt), which may involve substantial computational overhead for large k and t values.
